scenes.title: What is RISC Pipelining?
scenes.narration: RISC processors aim for single-cycle execution. By pipelining, the processor starts a new instruction every clock cycle, keeping hardware busy and increasing overall performance efficiency.

scenes.title: Three Pipeline Segments
scenes.narration: A typical RISC pipeline uses three segments: Instruction fetch, ALU operation for decoding or address calculation, and finally, execution to store results or access memory.

scenes.title: RISC vs CISC Pipelines
scenes.narration: RISC uses simple instructions requiring one cycle per segment. CISC uses more complex sets, often needing multiple segments and longer cycles to complete a single instruction.
